RL FILTER DESCRIPTION
A RL filter is a circuit constructed from inductors and resistors that will block certain frequencies and passes others.
DISCUSSION
The operation is based on how the inductor reacts to different frequencies, in other words, the inductor's reactance.
As you should recall, as frequency increases, inductive reactance increases.
You should also recall that the resistance of a resistor does not change when the input frequency changes.
Using these two concepts, filter circuits are very easy to understand, there is no new theory. You just put to use what you have already learned!
What does a RL filter circuit block or pass?
The definition of a RL Filter does not include blocking or passing voltage.

RL Filters come in two different configurations............
One configuration, called a low pass filter, passes low frequencies while blocking high frequencies.
The other configuration is called a high pass filter. It passes high frequencies while blocking low frequencies.
Let's discuss the low pass RL filter first.
A RL low pass filter consists of an inductor and a resistor.
The input is applied in series with the inductor. This is important for identifying a RL low pass filter.
The output is taken from across the resistor. This is also important for identifying a RL low pass filter.
The basic operation is that at low frequencies, L1 has a small inductive reactance.
The small XL does not drop very much voltage, most of the input signal reaches the resistor where the output is taken.
At high frequencies, L1 has a large inductive reactance.
Most of the input signal is dropped across the inductor and does not reach the output (the voltage across the resistor).

The high pass filter is discussed next.....................
A RL high pass filter consists of an inductor and a resistor just like the low pass filter.
The difference is that the input is applied in series with the resistor. This is important for identifying a RL high pass filter.
The output is taken from across the inductor. This is also important for identifying a RL high pass filter.
The basic operation is that at low frequencies, L1 has a small inductive reactance.
Most of the input signal is shunted to ground by the low reactance and not passed to the output.
At high frequencies, L1 has a large inductive reactance.
Most of the input signal is developed across the inductor and is passed to the output.
